issues.description: The server-side handling of POST /persons in the solution returns a plain Person (and returns null on invalid input) while the Note endpoints use ResponseEntity<T> and the problem statement shows the POST should return the saved person but also demonstrates ResponseEntity usage in similar endpoints. This inconsistent return type and error-handling style between NoteResource and PersonResource (and between the example pattern and the implementation) can confuse students about the expected response semantics and how to signal bad requests (e.g. returning null vs. ResponseEntity.badRequest()).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the POST /persons endpoint consistent with the other endpoints and the provided example: change createPerson to return ResponseEntity<Person>, and on invalid input return ResponseEntity.badRequest().build(), otherwise return ResponseEntity.ok(personService.savePerson(person)). This keeps response semantics consistent and avoids returning null for error cases.
